findings.title: 3-D GM = -0.115 (unstable) is refuted by an exact identity and by recomputation
findings.claim_under_review: GM (m) | ≈0 (neutral) | -0.115 (unstable)  +  2-D disk GM≈0 and 3-D sphere GM<0 are known analytical results

evidence.quote: - 2-D disk GM≈0 and 3-D sphere GM<0 are known analytical results; roll stability in ice fields comes from inter-particle contacts.

symbolic_identity.reading: GM = BM - BG identically 0 for a homogeneous sphere at ANY draught

nearest_standard_variant.formula: hemisphere BG taken from the keel at half draught (KG=R, KB=3R/8, BM=3R/8)

findings.reasoning: For a homogeneous sphere the waterplane second moment and the cap centroid satisfy BM = BG = 3(2R-h_c)^2/(4(3R-h_c)) identically (sympy residual 0), hence GM = BM - BG = 0 at EVERY draught: a negative GM is not attainable for the stated homogeneous body, so -0.115 cannot be a property of the model. The report's own 2-D column (GM≈0) and its 3-D column therefore contradict each other for two geometries that share the same identity, and the note calling GM<0 a 'known analytical result' is a misstatement.
findings.affected_scope: report 611 §3 GM row, §5 note 1; any downstream knowledge object that copies a roll-stability statement for DEM particles
findings.disposition: fix: recompute GM with a stated datum (KG, KB, BM) at the equilibrium draught; delete or correct the 'known analytical result' sentence; add GM to the error-assessment table

findings.title: the buoyancy verification is circular: 2.19e-16 is machine epsilon, so the check cannot detect model error
findings.claim_under_review: Buoyancy max rel error 2.15e-16 / 2.19e-16 with reference 'Archimedes', declared PASS
findings.reasoning: A relative error of 2.19e-16 = double epsilon can only be produced when the reference is the same algebraic expression as the result (my same-expression path returns exactly 0.0). Every genuinely independent reference is 7-12 orders of magnitude coarser: quadrature 1.19e-08 / 1.14e-10, Monte-Carlo 0.000973. So the check passes identically for a correct and for a wrong submerged-volume model; 'PASS' on this row is not evidence of fidelity. The report also never states an absolute F_b, so no dimensional/plausibility check is possible.
findings.affected_scope: report 611 §3 error row, §6 row 1, and the `All acceptance criteria PASS` conclusion
findings.disposition: fix: keep Archimedes as the model but validate against an independent reference (slice quadrature or Monte-Carlo, tolerances stated), and publish absolute F_b with units

findings.title: the Morison / wet-coupling half of the model carries no number, coefficient or environment in the text
findings.claim_under_review: the report is presented as a 'complete wet coupling model' with wave force verification

evidence.quote: - **Wave force:** Morison equation with Airy wave theory (deep-water decay)
- Morison equation valid for D/λ < ~0.1; at D/λ=0.1 we are at the upper limit.
See attached figures (6 total): submerged fraction, buoyancy force, wetted area, equilibrium diagram, heave stiffness, wave force time series.

findings.reasoning: No C_d, C_m, no wave-force amplitude, no wetted-area value and no water depth appears in the markdown, so the Morison branch is numerically unreproducible (evidence grade WITHHELD for that half of F07). Fig. 6 exists only as a caption; no data table accompanies it. D/λ from the stated lambda is exactly 0.1 but 0.1025 when lambda is derived from the stated T, i.e. marginally outside the validity bound the report itself quotes.
findings.affected_scope: §2 method bullets, §3 (no wave row), §4 figures, §5 notes
findings.disposition: fix: add C_d/C_m, wave-force amplitude table, wetted-area values and the water depth; state K-C number

findings.title: wave parameters lambda=10 m and T=2.5 s are mutually inconsistent in deep water (2.4-2.7 %)

evidence.quote: **Parameters:** R=0.5m, ρ_i=917 kg/m³, ρ_w=1025 kg/m³, g=9.81 m/s², wave A=0.1m, λ=10m, T=2.5s.

findings.reasoning: Deep-water dispersion with g=9.81 gives lambda=9.758 m for T=2.5 s (2.5 % below the stated 10 m), equivalently the pair implies g=10.053 m/s². Whichever is used, one stated parameter is inconsistent; downstream parameter cards must not copy the pair as-is.
findings.affected_scope: parameter list, and the D/λ validity statement
findings.disposition: fix: state T=2.53 s or lambda=9.758 m (or state the g used), keep the pair consistent

findings.title: 2-D heave stiffness is a per-unit-length (N/m²) quantity but is tabulated as N/m
findings.reasoning: Both numbers reproduce (3.2e-6 and 3.0e-5 relative), but a 2-D disk has no absolute stiffness: ρ_w g × width = 7414 N/m per metre = N/m². Putting the 2-D value (N/m²) and the 3-D value (N/m) in one column headed N/m invites a unit error in every downstream parameter card.
findings.disposition: fix: split the column into N/m² (per unit length) and N (per particle)

findings.title: two rows of the error-assessment table are not error statements
findings.claim_under_review: | Heave stability | k>0 | k=5081 N/m | YES |  and  | Equilibrium f_sub | ρ_i/ρ_w | 7.18e-13 | YES |

evidence.quote: | Heave stability | k>0 | k=5081 N/m | YES |

findings.reasoning: Row 2 compares the bisection result with the target it was solved for, i.e. a solver residual, not an independent validation (legitimate as convergence evidence, must be labelled as such). Row 3 states no error value at all while answering '<3%? YES'. The buoyancy/weight balance at the solved draught does close to 1.93e-16 relative, so the physics is fine; the defect is the form of the claim.
findings.disposition: fix: relabel row 2 as solver residual; give a numeric error for row 3
